thread:
maddie (AE): AstraMetrics just asked for a POC next Wed. They need steady 600 qps for chat completions (avg 90 tokens) and two 90s microbursts to 2.5k qps. Also strict p99 <= 350ms for user-facing flows. Can we assemble a plan and a quick price ballpark?
lee (SE): noted. need to confirm model family (7b vs 13b), whether they will use system prompts or long contexts. that affects KV cache hit-rate a lot.
sanjay (SRE): rough infra thought: sustained 600 qps w/ 7b-quant should be doable on 2 dedicated GPUs with good batching and hot KV. hitting 2.5k microbursts needs ~4 GPUs for headroom. will validate.
maddie (AE): they said they prefer lower cost so start with 7b-quant and sanity-check 13b impact. security requires SOC2 + CMK; may request HSM if they move to Private.
olivia (SalesEng): price ask: give 1) hosted pay-as-you-go estimate for their QPS profile and 2) a 6-month reserved Dedicated range with monthly cost. show math for GPU equivalent so procurement can compare.
lee (SE): testing plan I propose: warmup 15m; steady-state 45m at 600 qps; three microburst runs: 90s to 2.5k qps with 10m cool-down between; cold-start trial: restart pod then single 2m spike. Collect: p50/p95/p99/99.9 latencies, GPU util, batch sizes, KV hit percent, error rates, and queue lengths.
sanjay (SRE): add node-level traces and pod OOM/kern logs. tag metrics with model_variant and cache_key to attribute cache behavior. also capture request token histogram (in case they under/over estimate).
eve (Security): security checklist for AstraMetrics (short): SOC2 attestation yes; KMS w/ customer-managed keys optional; IP allowlist + mTLS; optional private VPC peering for Dedicated; retention policy for logs (default 30d) and option to purge; will need to review their security questionnaire.
maddie (AE): can someone prepare a 1-page checklist + test-run instructions I can send the customer this afternoon?
lee (SE): I'll drop the Locust + wrk lua scripts and a concise runbook. sample wrk invocation:
lee (SE): ```
w rk -t16 -c800 -d45m -s scripts/chat_test.lua http://<test-endpoint>
# script will send sampled prompts, include token counts and embellish to match production distribution
```
lee (SE): also include a small python harness to hit streaming endpoint for latency SLOs.
sanjay (SRE): cost sanity check: for 7b-quant, if they do steady 600 qps with avg 90 tokens and 2 microbursts monthly, hosted could be approx $0.018 per 1k tokens (ballpark) -> monthly depends on requests. For Dedicated reserved 24/7 sizing (~4 GPUs to cover bursts + headroom) expect $20k-$28k/mo depending on region and commit. 13b moves cost ~2x-2.5x. I'll run a sim and post numbers EOD.
olivia (SalesEng): include fallback routing note: we can auto-fallback to a lower-cost quantized variant or lower max tokens on overload. show them routing policy example.
eve (Security): add: if they require HSM-backed keys for inference-only encryption, that adds procurement time. flag to customer early.
maddie (AE): action list: lee = runbook + scripts; sanjay = infra sim + final price range; eve = security checklist doc; olivia = one-pager on routing/fallback. I'll book a customer kickoff for Wed 10:30am PT.
infra-bot: Test endpoint provisioning scheduled: https://staging.redwood.dev/astra/ by 2025-04-09T17:15:00Z
maddie (AE): perfect. I'll send checklist and NDA request to AstraMetrics and ask for a 24h sample traffic dump if they can share (anonymized).
lee (SE): quick note on metrics to capture during run (for the report): token/sec, batches/sec, avg batch size, model load times, prefix cache hit rate, queue time percentiles, system CPU steal, and GPU memcpy times.
sanjay (SRE): I posted preliminary sims in the ops doc (link). preliminary says 3x A10 equiv to be safe for 2.5k microbursts with <350ms p99 on 7b if caching is effective. otherwise nudge to 4 GPUs. will finalize numbers after a 2-hour load sim.
maddie (AE): thanks team. I'll forward the plan to AstraMetrics and confirm whether they want the 13b trials as part of the POC or as a follow-up.
lee (SE): will attach scripts in the next message. keeping test simple and reproducible helps procurement.
